children: Shares of Global Atomic were sharply lower Wednesday after the company priced a 50 million Canadian dollar ($35.5 million) public offering, diluting existing shareholders.
Shares fell 15% to 45 Canadian cents (32 U.S. cents).

The Canadian uranium company is raising money to continue developing its Dasa project in Niger, which it says will give it time to assess how to fund the remaining gap before drawing down on its U.S. International Development Finance contribution.

On Sept. 16, the company secured board approval from the Development Finance Corporation for a $414 million debt financing facility to fund construction for the project, but must fund its remaining equity contribution and meet local operational conditions in Niger, with whose government it co-owns the project, before drawing down the federal funds.

Global Atomic on Wednesday said that it would raise the C$50 million by issuing 100 million units of the company at a price of C$0.50 apiece, with each unit made up of one share and one-half warrant to purchase a share. Each full warrant is exercisable to purchase a share at C$0.70 at any time over the next three years.
The stock has been under pressure during all of 2026, falling nearly 38% to C$0.45 a share, including Wednesday's pullback.
Global Atomic has also granted its underwriters the option to purchase an additional 15% units to cover any surplus demand.
